description: A 64 by 64 grid of memory four planes deep, written and read at addresses given as voltages and shown on a lamp display, with the same memory offered to an expander placed immediately to its left

params.text: Adds to the X part of every address, 0 to 63 columns, and sets the whole X address on its own while nothing is patched to the X jacks
Adds to the Y part of every address, 0 to 63 rows, and sets the whole Y address on its own while nothing is patched to the Y jacks
Scales what is written into plane 0, 0 to 1, and sets the value written there on its own while nothing is patched to that plane's input, 0V to 10V
Scales what is written into plane 1, 0 to 1, and sets the value written there on its own while nothing is patched to that plane's input, 0V to 10V
Scales what is written into plane 2, 0 to 1, and sets the value written there on its own while nothing is patched to that plane's input, 0V to 10V
Scales what is written into plane 3, 0 to 1, and sets the value written there on its own while nothing is patched to that plane's input, 0V to 10V
Sets where the extra channels of a polyphonic write land when only one address is given: +0 puts them all in the same cell, +1 steps one cell along, +64 steps one row down
Chooses whether the row of channel lamps reports the cells being read or the cells being written
Chooses what the display shows: P3 shows plane 3 alone in green and red, RGB shows planes 0, 1 and 2 as red, green and blue, HSV shows those same three as hue, saturation and value
Scales the brightness of the whole display, 0 to 100 per cent, without changing anything stored
Chooses whether a write happens only while the write jack is above 0.5V, or on every sample whatever that jack reads
Sends the phasor input to the write address as well as the read address, which happens only while both write address jacks are empty; the lamp lights while it is happening
Sets every cell of all four planes to 0V, and springs back when released
Sets what may write to plane 0: Read-only lets nothing write, Write via DMA lets only an expander write, Read/write lets this module's own jacks write as well
Sets what may write to plane 1: Read-only lets nothing write, Write via DMA lets only an expander write, Read/write lets this module's own jacks write as well
Sets what may write to plane 2: Read-only lets nothing write, Write via DMA lets only an expander write, Read/write lets this module's own jacks write as well
Sets what may write to plane 3: Read-only lets nothing write, Write via DMA lets only an expander write, Read/write lets this module's own jacks write as well

inputs.text: Sets the X part of the read address, 0V to 10V across the 64 columns, added to the X knob; every channel patched here reads its own cell
Sets the Y part of the read address, 0V to 10V down the 64 rows, added to the Y knob; every channel patched here reads its own cell
Sets every cell of all four planes to 0V on each rising edge above 1V
Writes on each channel reading above 0.5V, and how many channels are patched here sets how many cells may be written at once
The voltage written into plane 0, multiplied by that plane's trimpot; its channels are written to the write addresses in turn
The voltage written into plane 1, multiplied by that plane's trimpot; its channels are written to the write addresses in turn
The voltage written into plane 2, multiplied by that plane's trimpot; its channels are written to the write addresses in turn
The voltage written into plane 3, multiplied by that plane's trimpot; its channels are written to the write addresses in turn
Sets the X part of the write address, 0V to 10V across the 64 columns, added to the X knob
Sets the Y part of the write address, 0V to 10V down the 64 rows, added to the Y knob
Reads a 0V to 10V ramp as a position through all 4096 cells, row by row, and breaks it into the X and Y phasor outputs

outputs.text: The value stored in plane 0 at the read address, one channel for each address being read
The value stored in plane 1 at the read address, one channel for each address being read
The value stored in plane 2 at the read address, one channel for each address being read
The value stored in plane 3 at the read address, one channel for each address being read
The X part of the position the phasor input has reached, 0V to 10V across the 64 columns
The Y part of the position the phasor input has reached, 0V to 10V down the 64 rows

notes: the memory comes up empty and the display stays dark until something is written; a write needs an address, a value from a data jack or a plane trimpot, and a plane switched to Read/write
with the read address jacks empty and the write address jacks patched, the read address follows the write address, so what was written can be read straight back
this module offers its four planes to an expander as four memory channels, reached by an Accessor or DMA-FX placed immediately to its left
a write also needs the write jack above 0.5V, or the write switch set to write always
menu: Fade lights — lets each lamp of the display slide towards its new colour instead of jumping to it, at the cost of redrawing the whole grid every 128 samples
Save memory contents — writes all four planes into the patch file, so what is stored comes back when the patch is loaded

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · stepped · polyphonic

unpatched it reads the X knob alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
